title: wolfSSL TLS 1.3 PQC hybrid KeyShare KyberKey error cleanup double-free
bug_class: TLS 1.3 PQC hybrid KeyShare error cleanup double-free
input_type: malicious TLS 1.3 ServerHello with truncated PQC hybrid KeyShare
notes: Candidate selected from wolfSSL official security vulnerability entry. Expected root cause: malformed TLS 1.3 PQC hybrid KeyShare triggers an error cleanup path that double-frees KyberKey / ML-KEM state.
crash_signal: AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free; WRITE of size 8; ForceZero -> TLSX_KeyShare_FreeAll -> TLSX_FreeAll -> wolfSSL_free; earlier free path includes TLSX_KeyShare_ProcessPqcHybridClient
fixed_behavior: wolfSSL_UseKeyShare returned 1; wolfSSL_connect_TLSv13 returned -1; wolfSSL_free completed; cleanup completed; NO_ASAN_CRASH_OBSERVED
current_behavior: wolfSSL_UseKeyShare returned 1; wolfSSL_connect_TLSv13 returned -1; wolfSSL_free completed; cleanup completed; NO_ASAN_CRASH_OBSERVED
reproduction_summary: A reconstructed malicious TLS 1.3 ServerHello contains a truncated PQC hybrid KeyShare for WOLFSSL_SECP256R1MLKEM768. The key_exchange length is 10 bytes, far shorter than the expected hybrid key share length. In v5.9.0-stable, wolfSSL_connect_TLSv13 fails and the later wolfSSL_free cleanup path reaches TLSX_KeyShare_FreeAll on already-freed key material, producing an ASan heap-use-after-free in ForceZero. In v5.9.1-stable and current, ownership cleanup is corrected and wolfSSL_free completes without sanitizer errors.
